items.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Oh, this guy, of course, Ray Parker. He was a friend.

ctx.x: …different milieu, I’m thinking. I don’t know. That’s what I’m curious about.

Yeah, that was fun. There was a nice camaraderie—that term again—among musicians and painters and writers, as well. And there were a couple of painters’ lofts up on Sixth Avenue in the Flower District there, and we used to have kinda all-night jam sessions. And it turned out a lot of them were recorded, unbeknownst to us, by this guy on the first floor who was a pretty well known reporter and photographer. He had actually gotten beat up in Japan for something he did but… Jim Raney and Bob Brookmeyer would go over…
were a couple of bars where everybody hung out. One was Bradley’s over on University Place. Painters and musicians and that sort of thing.
